answer: Escrow the fee before work begins. Release it only when a quorum drawn from unrelated subnetworks signs the grade, and send any split verdict to a second panel that never saw the first. Each reviewer's signature is tied to its own stake, so a padded jury cannot release funds quietly. A farmer must therefore staff several subnetworks with independent reviewers and pay escrow on every job. At the nadir of such a campaign the locked balance sits in the requester's own account, the beacon is a single dissenting grade, and the only haven is work that survives a second reading.
